execution/engine.notes: All 24 survivors are equivalent or unreachable. Three pass tool_calls=None instead of [] in the VOID, transport-failure and empty-response (T3-10) records: transcript.append writes None as []. One passes config=None to _build_messages, which does not use config. One replaces copy.deepcopy(messages) by copy.copy: the loop only appends to the list, never changes a message. Five change classify_attestation's arguments, which it ignores (always EV-1). Two drop the f'call_{turn}' default for a missing tool-call id and three change the '' default of tool_call_id in the tool message: a call without an id raises EngineError on the return-value lookup right after (S3-G2-2), so neither default is ever observed. Four change the defaults in current.get('choices', [{}])[0].get('message', {}) in the tool loop: only reached when the response has tool calls, so choices and message exist. Three change the '{}' default of arguments in _extract_calc_expression: None and 'XX{}XX' raise TypeError/JSONDecodeError, which are caught and give None, the same as '{}' (no expression). Two change the [] default of choices in _extract_tool_calls to None: both falsy, both give [].

execution/evidence.notes: All 8 survivors are equivalent. Six replace a .get() default by None or no default where the value is then only tested for truth or replaced by '' when falsy: 'content' in _extract_content, 'choices' and 'metadata' in extract_attestation (two mutants each). One makes the accumulated_tool_calls test always true: tc is then None instead of [], both falsy, so the final-response fallback and NOT-INVOKED follow the same way. One changes ranks_above's default rank for an unknown first argument from -1 to -2; an unknown first argument never ranks above anything either way.

execution/perturbation_guard.notes: All 32 survivors are equivalent: each changes the 'base' or 'removed' detail of a tools, tool_choice or sampling diff (key name, or the value looked up). Those details are never observable: a violation always raises PerturbationRefusal, whose message uses only each diff's 'field' and 'issue', and the diff list is only ever returned empty. _summarise itself is tested directly. (Step 5 seal-gt-guards, T3-46: identical prompts now raise, and the identical-prompt diff entry is gone; its 14 mutants were all killed, so removing them lowered the score from 163/195 = 0.8359 to 149/181 = 0.8232 with the same 32 survivors.)

execution/seal.notes: All 5 survivors are equivalent. 1 sets perturbed_any = None instead of False in perturbation_check: both are falsy, and the flag is only ever tested for truth. 4 replace the '' default of ap1_version_doi in verify_seal with None or no default, which is falsy like '' and skips the DOI check the same way. (Step 5 seal-gt-guards: the failure dicts no longer carry a 'field' key, which nothing read; every failure's item and reason are in the SealError message, S3-G3-3.)

execution/seal_constants.notes: No survivors. (Step 5 seal-gt-guards rewrote the check: failures are message strings, so the old survivors, renames of an unread 'reason' key, are gone. Legacy suites verify_d72b.py + verify_e7_coverage.py scored 0.7549 on the pre-step-5 mutants.)

execution/version.notes: All 12 survivors are equivalent. Three touch dead code: the local 'modified' (False to None or True) and the first 'result = {}' are assigned and never read. Three change the unreachable else of 'parts[0] if parts else ...' (a stripped non-empty line always splits into at least one part). Five change how VERSION is opened or a path is encoded: 'UTF-8' is the same codec; no 'r', no encoding or encoding=None mean the locale's, UTF-8 on macOS and Linux. One opens 'version' instead of 'VERSION', which macOS's case-insensitive file system finds anyway. No legacy suite imports version.py (0 % legacy coverage); the regression scenarios run it end to end.

foundation/adapter.notes: All 6 survivors are unobservable: they change the two request_record['attempts'] stores made just before raising (after the last transport failure, and the unreachable 'exhausted retries' path). That record is never returned or attached to the exception, so no caller can see it (finding S3-G1-18); the fix will make these mutants killable. The tests replace requests.post, time.sleep and time.time with fakes; the real HTTP path is covered by the regression scenarios against the mock endpoint.

foundation/config.notes: All 8 survivors are equivalent. Four change how config.json is opened: 'UTF-8' is the same codec, no 'r' is the default mode, and encoding None or no encoding means the locale's, which is UTF-8 on macOS and Linux (the tests load a non-ASCII config; on Windows these would be killed). Four change the .get() default for 'sampling' and 'quantisation' ({} to None or no default): both are required fields, checked present just before, so the default is never used.

foundation/numeric.notes: All 24 survivors are equivalent or unkillable. parse_decimal (7): is_neg=None is falsy like False; decimal_sep != 'XX.XX' only replaces '.' by '.'; the inner sign test 'XX-\u2212XX' only differs for 'X', which the outer test never lets through; sorting leading currency symbols by key=None or no key (4) is reverse alphabetical, and for startswith a symbol can only shadow another it is a prefix of, which sorts first either way. _build_extraction_re (2): key=None or no key for the alternation order is likewise equivalent (the regex backtracks; only a prefix can shadow). extract_numeric_tokens (9): currency_symbols=None reaches the same empty handling; finditer returns non-overlapping matches in order, so the dedup sort key (5 mutants) and last_end=-2 change nothing; every match contains a digit, so the 'no digits' guard and its continue->break (2) are unreachable. canonical_json ensure_ascii=None is falsy like False; canonical_hash 'UTF-8' is the same codec. file_hash (4): read(None) and read(8193) give the same digest; sentinel None or b'XXXX' never matches b'' and loops forever, which mutmut reports as a timeout.

foundation/transcript.notes: All 8 survivors are equivalent. Seven change how run.jsonl is opened ('UTF-8' is the same codec; no 'r' is the default mode; encoding None or none given means the locale's, UTF-8 on macOS and Linux, so the non-ASCII round trip passes; on Windows these would be killed). One passes ensure_ascii=None, falsy like False.

reporting/adjudication.notes: All 15 survivors are equivalent. One changes _needs_adjudication's figure_outcome default '' to 'XXXX', which is neither ADJUDICATE* nor UNMEASURABLE either. Two pass fixture=None and config=None to _generate_one_sheet, which never reads either parameter. Twelve replace a .get() default ([] or {} or '') by None or no default, falsy alike: account_map, tool_calls, operation_correctness, ungoverned_figures, choices and message content.

reporting/report.notes: All 51 survivors are equivalent. 34 replace a .get() default ({}, [], '' or False) by None or no default, falsy alike and only tested for truth: the summary's evidence_class_counts, item_evidence, transcription_results, release_coverage_results, invocation_figures, originated_operand_audit (twice), operation_correctness_counts, d1_results, d7_results, d2_results, surfaces, quantisation_findings, near_miss_findings, the dimension's results, operator_declared and a transcript record's evidence_class; one more changes that evidence_class default to 'XXXX', which does not contain UNOBSERVABLE either. Six are in the D7.3 percentage's else branch ('total > 0' to '>= 0', 'or True', the dash text), unreachable because the table is only built for a non-empty list. Seven change 'point = k / n ...' in the Clopper-Pearson section, a variable that is never read. One passes config=None to _section_preregistration, which never reads it; one passes ensure_ascii=None, falsy like False; one returns float('NAN'), the same value as float('nan'). [Integrator, step 5: re-recorded after merging the D7.1 and D7.3 fixes, 46 survivors; the notes above were written for one branch's 51 and were not re-audited after the merge.] [Integrator, step 5: re-recorded on the merge of the D7.1, D7.3 and seal-guard fixes; survivor notes not re-audited after the merge.]

run.notes: All 15 survivors are equivalent here. One passes argv=None straight to parse_args, which then reads sys.argv[1:] itself. Ten change how fixture.json and questions.json are opened: 'UTF-8', the locale default (UTF-8 on macOS and Linux) or no 'r' mode, and the upper-cased names, which macOS's case-insensitive file system finds anyway. Four change the default status of a result without one ('UNKNOWN', None, none, 'unknown'), all of which are scored.

runner/console.notes: The one survivor is equivalent: it changes the figure_outcome default from '' to 'XXXX', which takes the same branch (item answer incorrect).

runner/credentials.notes: The one survivor is equivalent: decode('UTF-16-LE') names the same codec as 'utf-16-le'. read_credential_windows is tested against a fake ctypes, so its Windows API use is checked by shape, not on Windows.

runner/executions.notes: Both survivors are equivalent. tool_calls=None in the figure record: transcript.append writes None as []. 'and' to 'or' in _operation_returns' result check only lets values through that then raise inside the try (a dict without 'result' raises KeyError), which the except turns into the same skipped call.

runner/outputs.notes: All 13 survivors are equivalent here. Twelve drop or change encoding='utf-8' on the four files written: 'UTF-8' is the same codec, and None or no argument means the locale's encoding, which is UTF-8 on macOS and Linux (the CI's Windows runs would differ; the regression baseline is made on macOS). One passes ensure_ascii=None, falsy like False.

runner/summary.notes: All 11 survivors are equivalent. Ten replace a .get() default ('' by None, 'XXXX' or no default) where every replacement takes the same branch: neither INVOKED nor NOT-INVOKED, not a counted provenance outcome, not starting AUTO or ADJUDICATE, no platform-rejected or platform-unsupported reason. One drops operator_declared=None, which is classify_mechanism's default. The module-level getcontext().prec = 50 is not mutated by mutmut; test_invocation_import_sets_global_decimal_precision_to_50 pins it (T3-60).

scoring/operation_correctness.notes: All 19 non-killed mutants are equivalent or message-only. 11 change the text of a ValueError raised in _eval_decimal, which evaluate_expression always swallows (returns None). In _floordiv (S3-G4-3): 'a <= 0' and 'b <= 0' for '< 0' (a == 0 leaves no remainder, so no adjustment either way; b == 0 has raised DivisionByZero before). In classify_operation: 'and' to 'or' in the expected-value conversion (None becomes Decimal('None'), which fails and gives None again), and two quantisation defaults ({} vs None, both falsy). In reclassify_session: 'er is not None or True' (Decimal('None') fails and gives None again), changed = None (falsy like False), and changed = True, an endless loop that mutmut reports as a timeout (the tests hang, so it is detected, but the score counts only kills). (Step 5 report-honesty removed evaluate_expression's unreachable 'if not isinstance(result, Decimal)' branch and its 4 survivors.)

scoring/provenance/classify.notes: All 5 survivors are equivalent. Two change the quantisation default ({} to None or no default): both falsy, both skip quantisation. Three change the '{}' default of arguments in _extract_expression (None, no default, 'XX{}XX'): each raises TypeError or JSONDecodeError, which is caught and gives None, the same as '{}' (no expression). Step 5 (d72a-fail-closed, T3-42) replaced classify_item's dead code (is_chained computed and unused, an empty 'if' block), which held 23 of the earlier 27 survivors.
